newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian minister says risk of civil war dimmed.
newsitem.headline: Albanian minister says risk of civil war dimmed.

text.p: The situation in the south of Albania is "completely out of control" but the risk of civil war has diminished, Albanian Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu was quoted as saying on Tuesday.

The leftist daily L'Unita reported Shehu as saying in an interview in Tirana on Monday that banks and libraries had been ransacked in Vlore and Saranda and a navy ship had been seized by "rebels" in the south.
However he said a state of emergency declared by the government had calmed the situation.

"With this ruling the risk of civil war has diminished hugely. If we had not taken it, do you know what would have happened? That today Tirana would have been attacked by the rebels," he told the newspaper in the interview on Monday.
"Up to now we have tried to act as prudently as possible to avoid armed clashes and bloodbaths. This line has not paid off and now the military operations start."
Asked whether this meant that the army would now attack the south, Shehu replied:
"Nothing of the sort. We will act calmly. It will probably take a few days to reinforce the law in Vlore. In the meantime, however, the rebels must hand over their weapons."

The Albanian government, facing violent unrest in the impoverished Balkan state, has issued orders to shoot armed rioters on sight, imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew and curbed press freedoms after parliament declared a state of emergency.
The unrest erupted after thousands of people were left penniless by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini was quoted as saying in La Stampa newspaper that Albania urgently needed a new democratic government in order to restore stability.
However Dini added he did not think that Albania was in a stage of pre-revolutionary ferment.
"I think that the most urgent thing for Albania is the formation of a new government, in which the democratic forces are fully represented," he said.
"It is a way of creating that political mobilisation that, alone, could allow a return to stability and the removal as soon as possible of the state of emergency," he said.
The rightist Democratic party of president Sali Berisha has 122 seats in the 140-member parliament.
The opposition refuses to take up the handful of seats it was allocated in the chamber after last year's general election, which was widely criticised by international observers.
The Albanian government of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi and his ministers resigned on Saturday. Opposition parties have called for the creation of a technocrat government to succeed them.
Dini said a new government was needed in Tirana because "if Europe does not have a valid partner in dialogue, it cannot carry out its own actions of support".
"Let us not forget that Albania is responsible for its own public order and a government is needed to guarantee it.
On Monday, Italy sent helicopters to Vlore, to evacuate 35 people, mostly foreigners, from the riot-torn port.
